title: Triggers Tutorial
description: Overview of SQL Server triggers including DML, DDL, and logon triggers.

data.text: SQL Server triggers are special stored procedures that are executed automatically in response to database object, database, and server events.

items: DML triggers — fired automatically in response to INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE events against tables.
DDL triggers — fired in response to CREATE, ALTER, and DROP statements.
Logon triggers — fired in response to LOGON events.

data.text: Inside a DML trigger, SQL Server exposes two special pseudo-tables: `inserted` holds the new rows and `deleted` holds the old rows. An `AFTER INSERT, UPDATE` trigger runs once per statement, after the change succeeds.

data.title: Audit new and changed orders
data.content: The trigger writes one audit row per affected order. Because it joins `inserted`, it handles multi-row statements correctly.

data.title: Do not assume one row
data.text: A single `UPDATE` can affect thousands of rows, and `inserted`/`deleted` will contain all of them. Set-based trigger logic is mandatory; a trigger that assigns `@id = (SELECT id FROM inserted)` silently loses rows. Also keep triggers short — they run inside the caller's transaction and hold locks while they execute.

data.title: Triggers Tutorial Key Points
points: Triggers are special stored procedures that execute automatically in response to events.
DML triggers respond to data modification events on tables.
DDL triggers respond to schema definition changes.
Logon triggers respond to user login events.
